public.prompt: A Vue 3 single-file component is the only place that renders `DateBadge`. Its descendants do not use that component, and the build should be able to omit it from entry points that never import this screen. Which registration expresses that dependency?

options.label: Register `DateBadge` with `app.component()` before mounting so every component in the application can resolve it.
Import `DateBadge` inside the screen's `<script setup>` and reference it directly in that screen's template.
Reference `<DateBadge>` in the screen template and rely on SFC compilation to discover and import the sibling file.

optionRationales.explanation: Global registration broadens availability to the whole application and can keep an otherwise unused component in the application bundle.
optionRationales.plausibility: An app-level registration lets any descendant template resolve the registered component name.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The dependency belongs to one screen and should remain explicit and locally tree-shakeable.

optionRationales.explanation: An imported component in `<script setup>` is available directly to that SFC's template, preserving a local and explicit dependency.
Vue does not discover sibling component files from template tags; the screen must import and expose or locally register `DateBadge`.
optionRationales.plausibility: Single-file component compilers resolve template syntax, so filesystem-based component discovery can appear built in.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The dependency must be explicitly imported by the only screen that uses it.

answerProof.summary: Vue SFC imports in `<script setup>` are locally available to that component's template, which keeps the dependency explicit without expanding registration to the application or descendants.
decisiveConstraints: Only the importing screen needs the component.
The dependency should remain visible to build-time tree shaking.
Descendant templates do not need inherited registration.

claims.statement: Components imported in an SFC's `<script setup>` can be used directly in that SFC's template as a local registration.
Local registration is scoped to the current component and does not make the component available in descendants, while global registration can inhibit tree shaking.
